visuals.title: Classic osteoporotic fracture sites
visuals.text: Vertebral wedge fracture (spine), Colles' fracture (wrist) and fractured neck of femur (hip).

visuals.title: Cancers that spread to bone
visuals.text: Breast, prostate, thyroid, kidney and lung (bronchus).

glossary.Pathology: Disease, or the study of disease processes in tissues.
glossary.Metastatic cancer: Cancer that has spread from where it started to other organs.
glossary.Low-impact trauma: A force that would not normally break bone, such as a fall from standing.
glossary.Hoist transfer: Moving a person with a mechanical lift; even this can break fragile bone.
glossary.Steroid: Glucocorticoid drugs such as prednisolone; long-term use thins bone.
glossary.BMI: Body mass index: weight in kg divided by height in metres squared.
glossary.Postmenopausal: After periods have stopped, when oestrogen levels fall.
glossary.Carcinoma: Cancer arising from epithelial cells, such as breast or lung.
glossary.Groin: The crease where the thigh meets the abdomen.
glossary.Urinary calcium: The amount of calcium lost in urine.
glossary.Neck of femur: The narrow part of the thigh bone just below the ball of the hip.
glossary.Primary tumour: The original site where a cancer began.
glossary.Bronchus: A main airway branching from the trachea into the lung.
glossary.Biopsy: Taking a small tissue sample to examine under the microscope.
glossary.CT: Computed tomography: X-ray-based cross-sectional imaging, good for bone.
glossary.MRI: Magnetic resonance imaging, good for marrow, soft tissue and spinal cord.
glossary.Immobilisation: Keeping a broken bone still, for example with a cast or sling.
glossary.Surgical fixation: Holding a fracture with plates, screws or nails.
glossary.Humeral shaft: The long middle part of the upper arm bone.
glossary.Closed fracture: A break where the skin is intact.
glossary.Sling: A fabric support for the arm.
glossary.Chemotherapy: Drugs that kill rapidly dividing cancer cells.
glossary.eGFR: Estimated glomerular filtration rate, a measure of kidney function.
glossary.Orthopaedic: Relating to the surgical specialty of bones and joints.
glossary.Stabilisation: Surgery to hold a broken bone firmly so it can bear weight.
glossary.Tumour infiltration: Cancer cells growing into and replacing normal tissue.
glossary.Mineralisation: Laying down calcium and phosphate crystals to harden new bone.
glossary.Resorption: Breakdown and removal of bone by osteoclasts.
glossary.Oestrogen deficiency: Low oestrogen, as after the menopause; removes a brake on osteoclasts.
glossary.Glucocorticoid: A steroid hormone such as cortisol or prednisolone.
glossary.Monoclonal antibody: A lab-made antibody that targets one specific molecule.
glossary.Renal function: How well the kidneys are working.
